title: Write-Execute computation: a Lean formalization of Self-Spectre with errata
abstract: Formalizes Gregory Morse's 2019 paper "Self-Spectre, Write-Execute and the Hidden State": the Write-Execute half unconditionally, the Self-Spectre half as conditional theorems over an abstract speculation contract. An ideal word-level machine whose only operations are a store and a jump, with no data reads, simulates finite Turing machines step for step, preserving halting, divergence and the tape; a finite image is exact until its guard faults. The development proves the jump-table lookup, the 8-bit tables, wide ADD, SUB, SHL, SHR, XOR, 32x32 multiplication, 64/32 division, two-step modular reduction, modular exponentiation with its multiplication count, the AES-128 T-table cipher and the Write-Execute AES procedure against FIPS-197. The Self-Spectre half is proved as a conditional result under an abstract speculation contract (a branch predictor and a speculation window as parameters, rollback of the architectural state, persistence of the cache): the Fig. 1 mistraining schedule, the Fig. 2 victim leak with the mix-order reload from a cleared probe array, the speculation-depth boundary (touch trace for any cache, observable reload hits from a cleared probe array) and the hidden Write-Execute computation. Supporting byte-level x86/x64 models of Figs. 5, 6 and 7 and native vectors for the corrected C and MASM sources accompany the selected statement.
